newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says Italy pension reform not issue at G-7.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy pension reform not issue at G-7.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi, asked to comment on calls for welfare reform by his treasury minister at Saturday's G-7 meeting, said on Sunday that any changes to Italy's social state would be decided in Rome.

Prodi, at his hometown of Bologna, was asked by reporters about remarks by Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi that European countries cannot afford to delay reforming their welfare systems any longer.

Ciampi, who said the matter had been touched on at the G-7 meeting in Berlin, had stressed that a balanced welfare system taking into account the steep rise in life expectancy in the past few years was "fundamental for financial stability over the long term."

Ciampi's remarks and similar comments in Berlin by Bank of Italy Governor Antonio Fazio were front-page news in Italy on Sunday, with newspapers speculating that changes were imminent to the country's generous pension benefits.

"I received a detailed and precise report on the meeting in Berlin. There was no reference to the problem of Italian pensions, it was a general discussion," Prodi said. "Pensions, social security and reform of the social state will be done in Rome, not Berlin."
WTO director-general Renato Ruggiero, who was in Milan on Sunday to attend a business seminar, said Ciampi and Fazio meant that European countries had to rethink not destroy their social states.

"We have to recognise that European countries have an economic growth of about zero and high unemployment while America came to the meeting with an economic growth of 4.7 percent and about 13 million new jobs, all created with salaries larger than our averages," Ruggiero said.
